title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the 'équation des lacets', a system (133)(134) for a pair (ξ,η) in the profinite fundamental group Π̂_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, which is free profinite on two generators. In the 'calcul adélique' he pushes this system through Π̂_{0,3} → Γ̂(2) ⊂ SL(2,Ẑ). The free group maps onto Γ(2)/±1, so the images in SL(2,Ẑ) are defined only up to sign. The previous page fixes the sign of ξ by (147), ξρ(η)ρ²(η)=±1. Writing ξ=(A B;C D) and η=(R S;T U), (147) becomes C+D−B=1 (150), with ξ ≡ 1 mod 2.

This page:
(1) The involution σ_∞ acts on SL_2 images as g ↦ ᵗ(g^{-1}), so σ_∞(η^{-1})=ᵗη. Relation (148), ησ_∞(η)=±1, therefore reads η=±ᵗη.
(2) The minus sign would force U=−U. Since Ẑ is torsion-free this gives U=0, contradicting η ≡ 1 mod 2 (R,U odd, S,T even). Hence η=ᵗη, i.e. ησ_∞(η)=+1 (151), i.e. S=T (152). The sign of ησ_∞(η) is insensitive to η ↦ −η, so this is a genuine constraint and not a convention.
(3) The loop relation (134) in SL_2 reads ξ = ε η (1 0; 2ν 1) = ε(R+2νS, S; T+2νU, U), with ε=±1 (153). Here (1 0;2 1)=y is the image of a generator and ν∈Ẑ is the exponent.
(4) Comparing entries gives B=εS and D=εU (154). Substituting into (150) and using S=T: C+D−B = ε(T+2νU+U−S) = εμU with μ=2ν+1. So the entry equation for C is equivalent to μD=1 (155), or μU=ε (155 bis).
(5) Next page: the A-entry then follows from the determinant relations, since D is invertible. The resulting theorem: μ=2ν+1 is a unit of Ẑ, determined by ξ (μ=D^{-1}) and by η up to sign.

Marginal note: with the chosen sign convention for η, actually ε=1.

Purpose: this extracts from the loop equation an 'abelian/SL_2 shadow', namely a unit μ∈Ẑ^*. It is the analogue of the cyclotomic parameter λ=2ν+1 in Drinfeld's ĜT, where λ∈Ẑ^* is likewise forced. This links his variant system to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group through the congruence/modular quotient.
errors: The overbrace labels are slipped. The terms ε(T+2νU), εU and εS are labelled A', B', C', but they are the entries C', D', B' of the right-hand side of (153). The paraphrase 'A+B−C=1' should be (150), C+D−B=1. The next page indeed labels ε(T+2νU) as C'.
The marginal 'Oups' records that the ε=±1 kept in (153) is in fact +1 under the sign convention adopted for η. The ± bookkeeping on this page is thus provisional or self-corrected.

Minor caveat: the sign of a lift is not detected mod 2 (−1 ≡ 1 mod 2); it would be detected mod 4. This explains why sign conventions must be fixed by (147) rather than by congruence. It is consistent with Grothendieck's remark that there is no simple way to lift the ambiguity.

ideas.what: Projecting solutions of a GT-type 'loop equation' in Π̂_{0,3} to SL(2,Ẑ) via Γ(2) and solving entrywise, with the sign ambiguity handled through ±1
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT-type elements under F̂_2 → Γ̂(2) ⊂ SL_2(Ẑ); modular/congruence quotient of ĜT
ideas.where_published: Spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, GT); the computation itself is in the unpublished Longue Marche follow-up notes

ideas.what: Symmetry η=ᵗη (S=T) forced by ησ_∞(η)=±1 plus η ≡ 1 mod 2 and torsion-freeness of Ẑ
Deduction that μ=2ν+1 is a unit of Ẑ, determined by ξ and by η up to sign
ideas.modern_name: Analogue of λ∈Ẑ^* (cyclotomic character) in Drinfeld's ĜT pair (λ,f)

missed.claim: Grothendieck works out in detail a variant system ('équation des lacets', involving σ_∞ and an exponent ν). In it, the cyclotomic-type unit μ=2ν+1 is recovered from the SL_2(Ẑ) image of the solution. This is a pre-Drinfeld-style derivation of the λ-component of a GT-like group. The specific computation on this page is elementary and unlikely to be new to specialists.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest. It documents Grothendieck independently isolating the 'λ ∈ Ẑ^*' part of GT-type equations through the congruence quotient.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine matrix computation within Grothendieck's unpublished GT-type investigations. Historically nice as a parallel to Drinfeld's λ, but mathematically elementary and conceptually known.
transcription_corrections: '(2)' throughout means 'mod 2', i.e. η ≡ 1 (mod 2), R,U ≡ 1 (2), S,T ≡ 0 (2).
Line labelled (151) reads: 'On a donc η = ᵗη i.e. ησ_∞(η) = +1', with (152) S = T.
In (153) a struck-out first factor (1 0; 2ν 1) on the left is deleted; the correct relation is ξ = ε η (1 0; 2ν 1).
The overbraces in the image are A', B', C' over ε(T+2νU), εU, εS (a slip by Grothendieck; they should be C', D', B').

Marginal note reads roughly: 'Oups ici ε=1, au vu de la convention choisissant le signe de η (la convention de signe ici n'est pas la même que celle considérée avant...; mais dans l'ensemble les points de vue présents sont plus symétriques)'.
